title: Multicenter study investigating the Single Question in Delirium in people with dementia
summary:
Recognizing an acute state of confusion (delirium) is particularly difficult in people with dementia, but is associated with significant negative consequences.. The Single Question in Delirium (SQiD) has proven to be a helpful tool in this regard. The aim of this study is to investigate whether the SQiD is also suitable for predicting the course of an acute illness in people with dementia, i.e., whether it can provide a prognostic statement.
The data collection is based on a prospective, multicenter survey of relatives of hospitalized geriatric patients with a known diagnosis of dementia. The SQiD question asks: "Is your relative currently more confused than before the hospital admission?" This question is part of the standard medical history interview and therefore does not represent an additional burden. The question is asked within 48 hours of hospital admission. The relative must have had sufficiently close contact with the patient beforehand to be able to answer the question.
The remaining data are taken from the patient's medical record.

interventions.name: Patients with dementia whose history from a next of kin answered YES to the Single Question in Delirium ("is your relative currently more confused than before the hospital stay?").
Patients with dementia whose history of the Single Question in Delirium ("is your relative currently more confused than before hospitalization?") was answered with NO by a a next of kin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatients with dementia
Exclusion criteria:
No relatives available for SQiD assessment; relatives who are not German-speaking.
